Thank you for the review.

Thank you for reviewing.

Good to see the robust discussion on this one. I think in the end, this get us somewhere better then where we are today, and given that Ed is a maintainer of EM, I think we just go with this proposal.

For requirement `4` i would like to propose doing this in `entity-manager` repository.

Initializing hardware and detecting hardware cannot really be separated well currently and there are proposals to initialize i2c gpio muxes and such from entity-manager as well (https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/entity-manager/+/75484).

Even if it is a separate daemon from entity-manager i believe it will be easier to coordinate this development in an existing repo close to the detection and configuration logic.

From my viewpoint there is a multi-stage initialization requirement.

- static detection 
- gpio initialization(your proposal?)
- dynamic detection (FruDevice, gpio presence, ...) 
- dynamic mux initialization
- dynamic gpio initialization
- possibly again dynamic detection
- possibly again dynamic initialization
- configuration
- sensor daemons

and EM may need to call into these custom initialization routines 
in case of dynamic initialization. Which is easier if that code is in the same repo.

Also there may be a preferred or required routine upon removal of a component which may require a custom de-initialization routine. That would also benefit from the code being available there.

> For requirement `4` i would like to propose doing this in `entity-manager` repository.

Agreed, this is likely where it would go, but this design doesn't cover those details, just use them as a future requirement for why this repo should exist.

> 
> Initializing hardware and detecting hardware cannot really be separated well currently and there are proposals to initialize i2c gpio muxes and such from entity-manager as well (https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/entity-manager/+/75484).

These are initting GPIO muxes based on detected components, this repo is for initting based on image defined rules.

> 
> Even if it is a separate daemon from entity-manager i believe it will be easier to coordinate this development in an existing repo close to the detection and configuration logic.
> 
> From my viewpoint there is a multi-stage initialization requirement.
> 
> - static detection 

This is intentionally not in EM today.  EM is for per-device configuration.  If you can "know" at an image layer that a software resource exists, ideally we shouldn't try to detect it in EM.

> - gpio initialization(your proposal?)

GPIO isn't unique here.  There's a lot more init that happens in platform init than just GPIO, and a lot of it requires a sequence or map of resources that can't be represented in an EM config.  For example

Standby power needs asserted
Wait for power good
Initialize sgpio
wait for sgpio good
Initialize GPIO expander
Read/write GPIO to init hardware.

> - dynamic detection (FruDevice, gpio presence, ...) 
> - dynamic mux initialization
> - dynamic gpio initialization
> - possibly again dynamic detection
> - possibly again dynamic initialization
> - configuration
> - sensor daemons

Yes, the rest is then handled by EM.

> 
> and EM may need to call into these custom initialization routines 
> in case of dynamic initialization. Which is easier if that code is in the same repo.

From the "explicitly out of scope" section in entity-manager:

"Entity manager shall not directly participate in management of any specific device"

https://github.com/openbmc/entity-manager/blob/master/README.md

> 
> Also there may be a preferred or required routine upon removal of a component which may require a custom de-initialization routine. That would also benefit from the code being available there.

Overall, this application exists because I don't see a way technically to make these things entity-manager enabled, and imposing a fru scanning requirement would reduce the reliability, as well as cause a deadlock (some FRUs are behind the Voltage regulator on this platform)

> Overall, this application exists because I don't see a way technically to make these things entity-manager enabled, and imposing a fru scanning requirement would reduce the reliability, as well as cause a deadlock (some FRUs are behind the Voltage regulator on this platform)

I mean it makes sense for simple initialization cases (single host, fixed board).
But if you consider blade servers too then these may need or want custom init routines aswell.

So the first initialization would need to be done before FruDevice as you said but blade initialization may need to be done based on dynamic detection.

My point is that there may need to be something in-between detection and EM exposing configuration. Which is the initialization step.

So having your code be in the EM repo would make it easier to call those handlers.


I believe your use-case is similar to the i2c mux feature which is also concerned
with initialization
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/entity-manager/+/75484

The major difference being the stage at which the initialization happens (before / after FruDevice) and how it is configured static/dynamic.

I see no reason why it cannot be supported to have a custom init routine for some hardware component after dynamic detection has started.


> Standby power needs asserted
Wait for power good
Initialize sgpio
wait for sgpio good
Initialize GPIO expander
Read/write GPIO to init hardware.

Many of your mentioned use-cases also apply after i2c muxes have been configured and dynamic detection has happened.

So these init handlers will also need to be available at that point and cannot just be something to run once then forget about it.

> "Entity manager shall not directly participate in management of any specific device"

Maybe it wont' be so bad if we have a simple handler architecture.
With ability to register fixed init functions based on the board
and then register init / de-init handlers based on `Type` of configuration and also based on individual boards (once detected, not-fixed init)

This may be useful in your case aswell. So you can do custom init based on
fields detected by `FruDevice` and handle some board variants/revisions differently.

Like this:

- fixed init hardcoded based on fw image
- FruDevice starts
- custom init based on fields from FRU Devices (handle board variants)
- EM exposes board inventory
- run custom handlers based on 'Type' of configuration
- (e.g. init i2c muxes, gpio expanders, ...)
- expose configuration record
...

For example in the ipmi stack they have a way to register custom handler functions and it does not make the core code any more complicated.

Since these handlers are all treated all the same with same function signature and so on.

> But if you consider blade servers too

For me that is outside the scope of this design.  I do not support blade servers, and presumably each blade would be a detected entity, so that would be a completely different design.

If the blade center needed their standby power brought up , that would be a good use case for this.

> Many of your mentioned use-cases also apply after i2c muxes have been configured and dynamic detection has happened.... cannot just be something to run once then forget about it.

All of the use cases mentioned for my platform are in fact run once and don't re-run until a reboot.


> Maybe it wont' be so bad if we have a simple handler architecture.

It's not about "being bad" it's about entity-manager being a common component that all systems can use, and application support being selectable based on component.

The point of this repo is for compile-time selection of init.  Entity-manager is for runtime selection of devices, and instantiation of inventory, both of which are not part of platform-init.


> So you can do custom init based on fields detected by FruDevice

This is very explicitly outside of the requirements.  Keep in mind, on some platforms the FRUs are actually behind initted hardware, so no FRUs are available until power rails are initted.

> For me that is outside the scope of this design. I do not support blade servers, and presumably each blade would be a detected entity, so that would be a completely different design.

> All of the use cases mentioned for my platform are in fact run once and don't re-run until a reboot.

So you are making something like a special purpose application which will likely only work for platforms similar to what you have.

Why not make something which fits your requirements but can be extended by others to fit their requirements also? 

> This is very explicitly outside of the requirements. Keep in mind, on some platforms the FRUs are actually behind initted hardware, so no FRUs are available until power rails are initted.

Yes the hardware can look however it was designed. Which is why we may need a flexible design which is not limited by it's own design to only run at the very beginning.


> The point of this repo is for compile-time selection of init. Entity-manager is for runtime selection of devices, and instantiation of inventory, both of which are not part of platform-init.

Compile-time selection of devices is just a fixed case of detection. There is no need to make any explicit distinction here? It is only a different source of information about which devices are present.

Custom init handlers generalize to both statically and dynamically detected devices. It is reasonable to only implement what you need (fixed initialization handlers) but i would love to see something which can be re-used and extended.

> > For me that is outside the scope of this design. I do not support blade servers, and presumably each blade would be a detected entity, so that would be a completely different design.
> 
> > All of the use cases mentioned for my platform are in fact run once and don't re-run until a reboot.
> 
> So you are making something like a special purpose application which will likely only work for platforms similar to what you have.
> 

I would say I'm making sure that I'm not just reinventing entity-manager/phosphor-inventory in a different form.  If multi-node makes sense to do as a fixed compile-time image thing, I'm open to seeing patches for it, I just don't have those requirements.  If there are things that need to be changed on reboot, those use cases are handled by other applications today (phosphor-state-manager for example).  The goal is not to duplicate function.

> Why not make something which fits your requirements but can be extended by others to fit their requirements also?

Overall, what you described is the intent.  This requirement set is intentionally minimal in the hope that we can get a home for some of the common init routines, and we can start accepting peoples init routines for other platforms.

> 
> > This is very explicitly outside of the requirements. Keep in mind, on some platforms the FRUs are actually behind initted hardware, so no FRUs are available until power rails are initted.
> 
> Yes the hardware can look however it was designed. Which is why we may need a flexible design which is not limited by it's own design to only run at the very beginning.


Concretely what changes do you think need made to the application to make a flexible design?  Could you put them in a gerrit review?  Some of what I want this repo for is so we can start to explore some of these ideas in code.

> 
> 
> > The point of this repo is for compile-time selection of init. Entity-manager is for runtime selection of devices, and instantiation of inventory, both of which are not part of platform-init.
> 
> Compile-time selection of devices is just a fixed case of detection.

I said selection of init.  This design has no concept of a "device".  If things can be modeled as a "device" that's detectable, I agree, that's where the line should end for this and entity-manager/reactors should begin.  In the examples in the repo today, compile-time selection is not just a fixed case of detection.

> There is no need to make any explicit distinction here? It is only a different source of information about which devices are present.

There are no distinction for "devices" here.  There is a known image that does known steps to init the platform its loaded on, no runtime detection.

> 
> Custom init handlers generalize to both statically and dynamically detected devices. It is reasonable to only implement what you need (fixed initialization handlers) but i would love to see something which can be re-used and extended.

My thinking was that this would look a lot like how qemu is setup.  There are routines for each platform

if (GB200){
   do_gb200_specific_things();
   do_common_thing_on_bus(2)
} else if (TyanS7106){
   do_tyan_specific_things();
   do_common_thing_on_bus(3);
}

Functions can be as common or as not common as we want them to be.  I'm not really sure what custom init handlers means in code, but I'm open to what it could look like.

> may need to happen any time a new hardware is added to the system

In my mind there's a large difference between "platform init" and "device init". A "platform" cannot be removed, it is a property of the image loaded.  I really think that runtime detection is well covered by entity-manager and reactors today, and I do want to draw some amount of a line to it's clear where each type of init "should" go.

> With this structure, init routines can be re-used for devices detected at runtime.

The code you posted looks like an improvement, but I'm not sure where the detection would happen or how it would happen?  I see a string for "TyanS7106" but it's not clear to me where fixed_device would come from?  If it's ultimately coming from a meson option, I'm in support of that model, and will pivot the code to do that once this repository is approved.  I don't have a detection requirement for the platforms that I would like this to target, so that might need to be a different design.

FWIW, two of the platforms I'd like to have common code for are actually Intel platforms not made by my employer, so I'm fairly sure there's some broad applicability.

> In my mind there's a large difference between "platform init" and "device init". A "platform" cannot be removed, it is a property of the image loaded.

I see no *fundamental* difference between a platform init and a device init which would *justify* any design constraint which may be limiting for OpenBMC in the future.

The platform is just a device which is known to exist and initialized first, before other devices. From BMC perspective the `platform` is always present.

> I do want to draw some amount of a line to it's clear where each type of init "should" go.

I am not sure where you would draw that line exactly? To me that sounds like some kind of discrimination where the platform is some kind of blessed device that gets treated differently?


>  If it's ultimately coming from a meson option, I'm in support of that model, and will pivot the code to do that once this repository is approved

Yes. The `fixed_device` string is coming from the fw image in my example. It's known beforehand and not detected at runtime.

> > In my mind there's a large difference between "platform init" and "device init". A "platform" cannot be removed, it is a property of the image loaded.
> 
> I see no *fundamental* difference between a platform init and a device init which would *justify* any design constraint which may be limiting for OpenBMC in the future.

Devices are detected at runtime, platforms are detected at startup.  That is why there are quite a few scripts now put into meta layers today.  Overall, I think this design is an improvement on what exists.

> 
> The platform is just a device which is known to exist and initialized first, before other devices. From BMC perspective the `platform` is always present.

The platform will not be self contained in a single inventory item, that is one of the distinctions that have put a number of scripts in meta layers.  The init scripts also don't host any telemetry or inventory, so enforcing that they do both of those would be a lot of effort.

> 
> > I do want to draw some amount of a line to it's clear where each type of init "should" go.
> 
> I am not sure where you would draw that line exactly? To me that sounds like some kind of discrimination where the platform is some kind of blessed device that gets treated differently?

Because we have different images per platform, that is already "blessed" by the project.  The goal here is to reduce the variability and copy-based between those already blessed images.

> 
> 
> >  If it's ultimately coming from a meson option, I'm in support of that model, and will pivot the code to do that once this repository is approved
> 
> Yes. The `fixed_device` string is coming from the fw image in my example. It's known beforehand and not detected at runtime.

Ok, so I think we're on the same page on that point.

> Overall, I think this design is an improvement on what exists.

Yes. Having a single application to put the init logic is an improvement and will lead to better re-use of common initialization routines. Error handling and logging of the init logic should also improve as a result.

100% agree on that. The C++ application is better than a bunch of copy-pasted shell scripts.

But we can go one step further and already think about enabling the next step which would require custom init handlers to be integrated with EM.

If you make a new repo it will make that next step that much harder and require to redo the whole thing again.

> 
> If you make a new repo it will make that next step that much harder and require to redo the whole thing again.

I'm not sure i understand why where the code is located makes turning this into an EM reactor in the future harder?  There are no EM reactors in the EM repo today, they're in dbus-sensors or individual repos.  Can you elaborate a little?

If someone has a design that they want to go through with that requires the code to move, I'm happy to even help move it, but as this design is defined (and carefully crafted to avoid scope creep) EM integration is not required, nor has requirements here.

> There are no EM reactors in the EM repo today, they're in dbus-sensors or individual repos. Can you elaborate a little?

`gpio-presence` is an EM reactor, right?

> I'm not sure i understand why where the code is located makes turning this into an EM reactor in the future harder?

Having more repos makes *everything* harder.

Needing more patches to get anything done.

If your proposed init code and entity-manager share the same repo, then someone can add both init and EM config for a platform in a single patch.

Which has the advantage that the platform does not get stuck in some stage where it has init but no config, or config but no init.

I'm not a fan of mono-repos.  I don't see a good overlap between this work and entity-manager.  We can always add service dependencies as/if needed to ensure we do the right thing here.  I think some platforms are going to be able to do their base-board detection without this code and some will not.  There probably isn't a strong tie between them.  More likely, fru-device might be precluded from running in some platforms until the initial init is done.

> I'm not a fan of mono-repos.

Grouping a few related features does not turn OpenBMC into a mono-repo.

> We can always add service dependencies as/if needed to ensure we do the right thing here.

systemd-level service ordering prevents the fine-grained ordering and may introduce some extra delay until `multi-user.target` is ready.

> I don't see a good overlap between this work and entity-manager.

Fine with me, since you agreed to help maintain/review this new repo.

I don't know if we have to support this now, but I'd also like this to be the place that we also add phosphor-state-manager hooks.  This might enable alternate executables and/or sub-commands.

1. Do you want to add a sentence about that now?
2. Should we make the executable be a sub-command for the "initial" init for the first go?

I'm 100% in support of that, but intentionally didn't add it because I didn't want to further complicate the doc.  If you think it's necessary to add a sentence to that effect for this to merge, I can do that, but I'd prefer to keep it to just init for now just for simplicity.

Happy to add a sub command (probably using cli11).   I think starting with something that doesn't parse CLI at all is easier as a first patchset, but I can put that up as a patchset in short order.

Does this document only cover the initialization portion or do we want to cover all power on/off/cycle too? 

Could we potentially have our "platform_power_control" link to phosphor-state-manager through dbus so we can have custom init, on, off, etc in C++?

> Does this document only cover the initialization portion

For now.... yes.  Based on talking with folks, I think there's some broad agreement that could be reached about power operations as well, but in was intentionally left out.

> could we

it's software, anything is possible, and what you suggested has been suggested by others as well.
I'd prefer we drop this.  No reason to also support bash.

My thinking was that step 1 was to get all the bash scripts into one place so people quit extending and copy/pasting them, then step 2 was to start conslidating them porting them into this application.  Lots of issues stem from folks just copying scripts in the tree without realizing they're maybe not the best, so my hope was to improve that, but sure, I can remove this.

With all that said, I've dropped this sentence.

I see that "detection" is left as a future exercise.  Do we want to remove the meson option and compile all platforms in, but have the platform as an argument in the service file?  We can default to "detect" (which is maybe a no-op for now).

My original thinking was that if we have to pull in an odd dependency, like peci-utils, you probably don't want to have that dependency on a non-intel platform, but sure, I think we can start with just including all platforms and handle that case when and if it comes up.

I've updated the doc to swap meson option -> CLI option.

Let's not from the get-go make it optional.
If it ends up being a big binary then maybe?

There is currently so much optionality in OpenBMC that it is leading to incompatibility between components.

> Let's not from the get-go make it optional.

In the initial, SOME platform will need to be opt in.  I agree, ideally we'd enable this everywhere, and for platforms that don't have definitions would just a be no-op.

> If it ends up being a big binary then maybe?
> 
> There is currently so much optionality in OpenBMC that it is leading to incompatibility between components.

There's pros and cons to optionality.  From my perspective, I'd like to see common solutions where there are common problems that can be solved once.  There's a lot more routines that can be made common by creating this platform init common application.

> In the initial, SOME platform will need to be opt in.

What about making it opt-out.

> What about making it opt-out.

Can't do that until we have something that works, then yes, I would advocate for it being opt-out.
Acknowledged

If there is a new repo, please have at least 2 maintainers, preferably from 2 different companies.

To provide a balanced viewpoint in the code review process and ensure the knowledge about how the thing works is not contained in just one person.

> If there is a new repo, please have at least 2 maintainers, preferably from 2 different companies.
> 
> To provide a balanced viewpoint in the code review process and ensure the knowledge about how the thing works is not contained in just one person.

That's fine, and I'm in support, but without someone volunteering this comment isn't really actionable.

We also haven't enforced that in the past, and there are a number of repos that are single active maintainer.  Doing as you ask is certainly something to discuss, but I would ask that it doesn't block this review specifically.

> We also haven't enforced that in the past

Then why not start this good habit now 😊

> That's fine, and I'm in support, but without someone volunteering this comment isn't really actionable.

I can volunteer to look at the init code if we can get it into `entity-manager` repo and not create yet another one.

Since initialization and configuration are closely related and need to be coordinated well, i believe this application can go into `entity-manager` repo.

Also i believe the benefit of having more people to maintain this thing outweighs any benefits a separate repo could provide.

> > We also haven't enforced that in the past
> 
> Then why not start this good habit now 😊
> 

Because it's a separate concern.  Many people would debate "good".

> > That's fine, and I'm in support, but without someone volunteering this comment isn't really actionable.
> 
> I can volunteer to look at the init code if we can get it into `entity-manager` repo and not create yet another one.
> 
> Since initialization and configuration are closely related and need to be coordinated well, i believe this application can go into `entity-manager` repo.


As the entity-manager maintainer, I would like to maintain the rule that EM does not participate in hardware management itself.  I do not see how technically one could integrate this application with EM.  Doing so would involve blocking the main dbus reactor, which would be bad for dbus response times.  This application proposed doesn't have a dbus interface.

> 
> Also i believe the benefit of having more people to maintain this thing outweighs any benefits a separate repo could provide.

I would love to see more people maintain this.  And FWIW, once i get the GPIO things solved, the next thing in my targets are the duplicated host interface scripts:
https://github.com/openbmc/openbmc/blob/master/meta-fii/meta-kudo/recipes-kudo/network/usb-network/usb_network.sh

That should all be common.  I would expect to see a lot more maintainers be involved once that happens, but at the moment, I need to get the existing code moved to place that can be maintained at all (not in a company-specific meta layer).

> As the entity-manager maintainer, I would like to maintain the rule that EM does not participate in hardware management itself. 

Then it will need to be handled with IPC which is even more complicated.
I thought the intend behind the rule was to keep EM simple.
Extra IPC interfaces are the opposite of that.

> I do not see how technically one could integrate this application with EM. Doing so would involve blocking the main dbus reactor, which would be bad for dbus response times. This application proposed doesn't have a dbus interface.

Setting a few gpios as part of initializing a blade should not take too long?
Otherwise, the init can be done in a separate process which is spawned and we can async wait for it to complete?

> I would love to see more people maintain this.

Which is at odds with creating new repositories. Creating a lot of busy work and boilerplate code instead of leveraging an existing repo.

From my perspective, starting a new repo with no other reviewers is just a way of sidestepping the community code review process.

> > As the entity-manager maintainer, I would like to maintain the rule that EM does not participate in hardware management itself. 
> 
> Then it will need to be handled with IPC which is even more complicated.
> I thought the intend behind the rule was to keep EM simple.
> Extra IPC interfaces are the opposite of that.

It's not clear where this IPC is coming from?  There is currently no IPC in this design, by design.  The moment we get into needing dbus/ipc/state, the design doesn't belong in this repo/application.

> 
> > I do not see how technically one could integrate this application with EM. Doing so would involve blocking the main dbus reactor, which would be bad for dbus response times. This application proposed doesn't have a dbus interface.
> 
> Setting a few gpios as part of initializing a blade should not take too long?

This design and application does more than set GPIOs.  There are cases where it needs to wait for GPIOs to assert, that does take some time.

> Otherwise, the init can be done in a separate process which is spawned and we can async wait for it to complete?

That design would make this a full reactor, and largely defeat the purpose of doing a known initialization.

> 
> > I would love to see more people maintain this.
> 
> Which is at odds with creating new repositories. Creating a lot of busy work and boilerplate code instead of leveraging an existing repo.
> 
> From my perspective, starting a new repo with no other reviewers is just a way of sidestepping the community code review process.

FWIW, this was discussed some in TOF, and creating a new repository was what was asked for.  This code is currently in a meta layer, which is even worse than a common repo with one maintainer.  I'm actually hoping that by pulling in use cases into a common repo instead of putting it in meta layer scripts that they get more scrutiny and review, not less.

The structure I'd really like to see in this repo is that each platform is in a folder, and each platform maintainer is in the OWNERS for that folder.  Common layers will be reviewed by all platform maintainers that pull in the common components.

Overall, this is something that I think the project needs, and I'm open to having other maintainers.  The only reason I'm requesting a new repo is that there wasn't a logical place to put general hardware init code.  Most thusfar have been putting it in meta layers, which makes it harder to share.

> The only reason I'm requesting a new repo is that there wasn't a logical place to put general hardware init code.
